explanation: This pole is a retrospective, token-local lexical detector for one English 'becoming more' verb cluster: it peaks (2.1-4.2 on a 4.2 scale) exactly on the current token when that token is an inflected form of raise, rise, grow, gain, draw or gather (raise/raised/raising/raises, rise/rose/risen/rising/rises, grow/grew/grown/growing/grows/growth, gain/gained/gains/gaining, draw/drew/drawn/draws/drawing, gather/gathered/gathers/gathering), gives a middle band of about 1.0-2.1 to their close 'bring forth / come into being / go up' relatives (yield, garner, amass, arose/arisen/arising, sprang/sprung, derive, generate, source, born, climb, mount, arouse, increase/increased/increasing, more weakly collect), and stays at or near zero (<=0.9, mostly exactly 0.00) for other near-synonyms of increase or upward motion (boost, expand, double, jump, soar, surge, improve, elevate, lift, produce, ask, pose, provoke, fall/fell, drop, decline, reduce, lower, cut) and for orthographic neighbours (praise, raisin). Everything else in the sentence reads exactly 0.00, so the object, the syntax, the direction of the change and the following word never modulate it: the current word form alone sets the strength, plus a small (+0.5-1.1) boost when that token comes later in the sentence after an auxiliary or infinitival 'to', and the negative pole is a flat -0.10 to -0.17 with no structure; there is no lookahead, since the Jacobian lens promotes the same family (growth, Heights, height, ascent, yield) but at kurtosis 3.3 with 0% lens agreement, i.e. no specific next-token prediction.
